subject: Model fit mediation model categorical outcome

messages.author: 57adfeaf6a74fec2
messages.subject: Model fit mediation model categorical outcome
parts:
Hi,

I'm conducting a mediation analysis with a categorical outcome. The model fit shows a saturated model. I have figured out that this has something to do with the amount of explanatory variables and data points. Only, when I exclude the direct path: X -> Y the model shows a CFI and TLI of .925 (not acceptable). However, I read an article that cutoff criteria for models with catergorical outcomes should be interpreted with caution. And I saw another comment somewhere, that you shouldn't worry too much about the model fit.

How can I deal with this model fit? I do need the c' path, so do I report the saturated model, and how?

Hope someone has some suggestions.

KR. Angela

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Model fit mediation model categorical outcome
parts:
This isn't a categorical-data issue.

Do you have just X, M, and Y? If so, the only way to not have a saturated model is to, as you tried, omit the X->Y path. But is this conceptually reasonable in your case? If it isn't, then don't exclude it. Just live with your (non-falsifiable) saturated model. If you have other variables that might not be in saturated relations with X, M, and Y, you may be able to learn more from your data.

Also, this is a general SEM question, not lavaan, so SEMNET may give you a fuller answer. https://listserv.ua.edu/archives/semnet.html

Pat
